question_html: What is the key difference between the dissolution of a partnership and the dissolution of a partnership firm?

options.A: Dissolution of partnership involves closing all books, whereas dissolution of a firm does not.
options.B: Dissolution of a partnership represents a reconstitution of the firm, whereas dissolution of a firm implies that the entire firm ceases to exist[cite: 25].
options.C: Court intervention is mandatory for dissolution of a partnership.
options.D: Assets are revalued on dissolution of a firm and sold on dissolution of a partnership.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Dissolution of the firm implies that the entire firm ceases to exist, including the relation among all the partners, whereas dissolution of partnership refers to discontinuance of relation or reconstitution[cite: 25].
topic_text: Distinction between Dissolution of Partnership and Dissolution of Partnership Firm

question_html: Under Section 48 of the Indian Partnership Act, in what order are the assets of the firm (including sums contributed by partners for capital deficiencies) applied upon dissolution?

options.A: 1. Capital contribution, 2. Third-party debts, 3. Advances
options.B: 1. Debts to third parties, 2. Rateable advances/loans from partners, 3. Capitals, 4. Residue in profit-sharing ratio[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (B) Assets are applied in paying third-party debts, rateable advances from partners, capital balances, and residue among partners in profit-sharing ratio[cite: 25].

question_html: Which account is prepared to close the books of accounts upon the dissolution of a partnership firm?

options.A: Revaluation Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Realization Account is prepared at the time of dissolution of a partnership firm[cite: 25].

question_html: What type of account is a Realization Account?

options.A: Nominal Account[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) Realization Account is a nominal account[cite: 25] used to record realization of assets and discharge of liabilities.

question_html: How is an unrecorded asset realized at the time of dissolution treated in the ledger accounts?

options.A: Debited to Realization Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) An unrecorded asset realized at the time of dissolution is credited to Realization Account[cite: 25].
topic_text: Treatment of Unrecorded Assets on Realization

question_html: When a liability is taken over by a partner at the time of dissolution, which account is credited?

options.A: Profit and Loss Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) A liability taken over by a partner is credited to Partners' Capital Accounts and debited to Realization Account[cite: 25].

question_html: Which methods are adopted for piecemeal distribution of cash among partners to ensure distributions are in proportion to their interest?

options.A: Maximum loss method and Highest relative capital method[cite: 25]
options.C: Surrender value method and Reserve method
options.D: Average profit method and Super profit method

answer_html: Answer: (A) Piecemeal distribution involves either maximum loss method or highest relative capital method[cite: 25].

question_html: What rule governs the treatment of capital deficiency when a partner becomes insolvent during dissolution, in the absence of a specific partnership agreement?

options.A: Rule in Garner vs. Murray[cite: 25]
options.B: Rule in Section 37 of Partnership Act

answer_html: Answer: (A) The loss arising from insolvency of a partner is borne by solvent partners following the decision in Garner vs. Murray[cite: 25].
topic_text: Insolvency of Partner and Garner vs. Murray

question_html: Under the rule in Garner vs. Murray, how do solvent partners bear the capital deficiency of an insolvent partner?

options.A: In their profit-sharing ratio
options.D: In the ratio of their drawings

answer_html: Answer: (B) Solvent partners bear the capital deficiency of an insolvent partner in proportion to their capitals[cite: 25].
topic_text: Garner vs. Murray Capital Ratio Principle

question_html: Under what circumstances is the rule in Garner vs. Murray NOT applicable?

options.A: When a solvent partner has a debit balance in capital account[cite: 25]
options.B: When there are three partners in the firm
options.D: When assets are sold in installments

answer_html: Answer: (A) Garner vs. Murray rule is not applicable when a solvent partner has a debit balance in their capital account, when there are only two partners, or when there is a contrary agreement[cite: 25].

question_html: Can a court order the dissolution of a partnership firm if a partner becomes of unsound mind?

options.A: Yes, court has the power to order dissolution[cite: 25]
options.B: No, court cannot interfere in partnership matters
options.D: Only after expiry of a fixed term

answer_html: Answer: (A) The court has the option to order dissolution where a partner has become of unsound mind[cite: 25].

question_html: When all partners of a firm are insolvent, where is the balance of creditors' accounts transferred instead of the Realization Account?

options.A: Deficiency Account[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) When all partners are insolvent, it is better not to transfer creditors to Realization; instead, the balance is transferred to Deficiency Account[cite: 25].

question_html: How is purchased goodwill appearing in the balance sheet treated upon dissolution of a firm?

options.A: Treated like any other asset and transferred to Realization Account[cite: 25]
options.C: Transferred directly to partners' capital accounts in profit-sharing ratio
options.D: Retained as an intangible asset in the final balance sheet

answer_html: Answer: (A) If goodwill appears in the Balance Sheet, it is considered purchased goodwill and treated like any other asset by transferring to Realization Account[cite: 25].

question_html: Can the winding up of a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) be initiated by the Tribunal if the LLP has less than 2 partners for more than 6 months?

options.A: Yes[cite: 25]
options.C: Only if partners agree in writing

answer_html: Answer: (A) Winding up of an LLP may be initiated by the Tribunal if the LLP has less than 2 partners for more than 6 months[cite: 25].

question_html: Are books of accounts closed in the event of dissolution of a partnership versus dissolution of a partnership firm?

options.A: Books are not closed in dissolution of partnership, but books are closed in dissolution of a partnership firm[cite: 25].
options.B: Books are closed in both cases.
options.C: Books are never closed upon dissolution.
options.D: Books are closed only for LLPs.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Books of accounts are not closed in dissolution of partnership, whereas they are closed in dissolution of a partnership firm[cite: 25].

question_html: In Fast and Quick (sharing 3:2), assets transferred to Realization were ₹90,000, creditors ₹20,000, provision for doubtful debts ₹1,000. Assets realized ₹85,500, creditors paid ₹19,000, realization expenses ₹3,500, and Fast took over patents at ₹5,000. What is the net profit or loss on realization?

options.A: Loss of ₹1,000[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in text Section 6.4, the Realization Account shows a net loss of ₹1,000 distributed between Fast (₹600) and Quick (₹400)[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 1 (X, Y, Z sharing 4:3:2, fixed assets ₹5,00,000, stock ₹3,00,000, debtors ₹5,000,000), fixed assets realized ₹5,20,000, book debts ₹4,40,000, stock taken over by Y at ₹2,50,000, creditors of ₹3,20,000 paid at 5% discount, expenses ₹6,000. What is the total loss on realization?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total realization loss = ₹35,555 (X) + ₹26,667 (Y) + ₹17,778 (Z) = ₹80,000[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 1, what amount is finally paid to partner X on Capital Account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Partner X receives ₹4,04,445 as final cash settlement on capital account[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 2 (P, Q, R sharing 3:2:1, fixed capitals P:20,000, Q:20,000, R:10,000), R became bankrupt and could bring only 1/3 of the amount due. Under Garner vs. Murray, how is R's capital deficiency borne by solvent partners P and Q?

options.A: In their fixed capital ratio (2:2 or 1:1)[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) Following Garner vs. Murray rule, solvent partners P and Q bear R's deficiency in their fixed capital ratio (20,000:20,000 = 1:1)[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 3 (Amal and Bimal in equal partnership, total creditors ₹4,800, plant & machinery ₹2,500, furniture ₹500, debtors ₹1,000, stock ₹800), total assets realized ₹2,300, realization expenses ₹175, and creditors paid ₹2,525. What is the total loss on realization?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Realization loss is ₹2,675, shared equally between Amal (₹1,337) and Bimal (₹1,338)[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 4 (A, B, C, D sharing 4:3:2:1), D became insolvent and a dividend of 25 paise in a rupee was received. Total realization loss was ₹23,050. What is D's total deficiency transferred to solvent partners?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Total amount due from D was ₹10,720; 25% (₹2,680) was recovered from estate, leaving an unrecovered deficiency of ₹8,040 borne by solvent partners A and B[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 5 (X, Y, Z sharing 2:2:1, Y insolvent), unrecorded purchases of ₹4,000 were discovered. What is the total realization loss distributed among X, Y and Z?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total realization loss is ₹24,000, shared as X: ₹9,600, Y: ₹9,600, Z: ₹4,800[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 6 (A, B, C sharing 5:3:2, capitals ₹9,600, ₹6,000, ₹8,400, B insolvent), maximum possible loss method is used for piecemeal distribution. After all assets are realized and maximum possible loss is allocated, how is B's deficiency treated?

options.A: Written off against C (solvent partner)
options.C: Borne equally by A and C

answer_html: Answer: (A) B's deficiency is written off against C in capital ratio[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 7 (A, B, C sharing 2:2:1, capitals A:15,000, B:18,000, C:9,000), when applying the Highest Relative Capital Method, what is the proportionate capital of B and C taking A's capital base (15,000) and profit sharing ratio (2:2:1)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Proportionate capitals taking A as base are B: ₹15,000 and C: ₹7,500[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 8 (A, B, C sharing 2:2:1, capitals A:76,000, B:48,000, C:36,000), who has the least capital per unit of profit share (capital / profit share)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) B has the least capital per unit of profit share (₹24,000), so B's capital is taken as the basis[cite: 25].

question_html: In Illustration 9 (P & Q sharing equally in LLP, P capital ₹1,00,000, Q capital ₹50,000, creditors ₹20,000, reserves ₹15,000), P took over 50% stock at 10% less than book value. If total stock was ₹35,000, what is the value at which P took over 50% stock?
answer_html: Answer: (A) 50% of stock = ₹17,500. Less 10% discount = ₹17,500 - ₹1,750 = ₹15,750[cite: 25].

question_html: In Practical Question 1 (P, Q, R sharing 2:2:1, plant & machinery ₹1,08,000, fixtures ₹24,000, stock ₹60,000, debtors ₹48,000), assets realized: plant ₹1,02,000, fixtures ₹18,000, stock ₹84,000, debtors ₹44,400, and unrecorded asset taken over by Q at ₹4,800. What is the total cash realized from assets?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total cash from asset realization = ₹1,02,000 + ₹18,000 + ₹84,000 + ₹44,400 = ₹2,48,400[cite: 25].

question_html: In Practical Question 2 ('Thin', 'Short' and 'Fat' sharing 2:2:1, Thin and Short solvent, Fat has no private assets and is insolvent), how is Fat's capital deficiency borne by Thin and Short under Garner vs. Murray?

options.A: In their fixed capital ratio (8:5)[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) Fat's deficiency is borne by Thin and Short in their fixed capital ratio (80,000 : 50,000 = 8:5)[cite: 25].
topic_text: Practical Question 2 Garner vs Murray Deficiency Ratio

question_html: In Practical Question 3 (Amit, Sumit, Kumar sharing 2:2:1, bills payable ₹12,000 due in 1 month paid immediately on 31st March at 6% p.a. discount), what amount is paid in cash for bills payable?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Discount for 1 month = $12,000 \times \frac{6}{100} \times \frac{1}{12} = \text{₹}60$. Cash paid = ₹12,000 - ₹60 = ₹11,940[cite: 25].

question_html: In Practical Question 3, trade creditors of ₹30,000 agreed to take over furniture of book value ₹12,000 at ₹10,800, and remaining creditors were paid off at a discount of 6.25%. What amount is paid in cash to trade creditors?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Remaining creditors = ₹30,000 - ₹12,000 = ₹18,000. Less 6.25% discount (₹1,125) or net settled at ₹18,000 cash[cite: 25].

question_html: When a partner pays a premium upon admission with a stipulation that the firm will not be dissolved before a fixed term, and the firm is dissolved before the term expires, what is the partner entitled to?

options.A: A suitable refund of premium or reasonable part thereof[cite: 25]
options.D: Full refund of capital plus interest

answer_html: Answer: (A) A partner who pays a premium with a stipulation that the firm will not dissolve before a fixed term is entitled to a suitable refund of premium if dissolved prematurely[cite: 25].
topic_text: Refund of Premium on Premature Dissolution

question_html: Under what condition will NO claim for refund of admission premium arise if a firm is dissolved before the expiry of a fixed term?

options.A: If dissolution is due to death of a partner, own misconduct, or agreement containing no refund provision[cite: 25]
options.B: If dissolution is ordered by the court due to partner insanity
options.C: If all creditors agree to extension
options.D: If assets realize more than book value

answer_html: Answer: (A) No claim arises if dissolution is due to death, partner's own misconduct, or agreement containing no provision for return[cite: 25].

question_html: When preparing a Realization Account, which of the following accounts should NOT be transferred to the Realization Account?

options.A: Cash or Bank Balance, Debit/Credit Balance of P&L A/c, Partners' Current, Capital, and Loan A/cs[cite: 25]
options.B: Plant and Machinery, Stock, Sundry Debtors
options.C: Sundry Creditors and Provision for Doubtful Debts

answer_html: Answer: (A) Cash/Bank, accumulated P&L balances, partners' current, capital, and loan accounts are not transferred to Realization Account[cite: 25].

question_html: How is a partner's loan/advance treated during the final settlement of accounts upon dissolution, as distinguished from capital?

options.A: Paid off after third-party debts but before repayment of capital[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) Partner's loans/advances are paid off after third-party debts and before repayment of capital[cite: 25].

question_html: When capitals are fluctuating, how is the capital ratio for bearing insolvency loss (Garner vs. Murray rule) determined?

options.A: After adjusting all reserves, accumulated profits, drawings, and interest up to dissolution date, but before profit/loss on realization[cite: 25]
options.B: Based on opening capitals of the year
options.C: Based on final capital balances after realization

answer_html: Answer: (A) Capital ratio is determined after adjusting reserves, accumulated profits, drawings, interest up to dissolution, but before realization profit or loss[cite: 25].

question_html: What is the effect on the Realization Account when realization expenses are paid by the firm?

options.A: Realization Account is debited and Cash/Bank Account is credited[cite: 25]
options.B: Cash Account is debited and Realization Account credited
options.C: Partners' Capital Accounts are debited directly

answer_html: Answer: (A) Realization Account is debited and Cash/Bank Account credited for payment of realization expenses[cite: 25].

question_html: If a partner agrees to bear realization expenses in exchange for a fixed remuneration, what amount is debited to the Realization Account?

options.A: The fixed remuneration agreed upon with the partner[cite: 25]
options.B: The actual expenses incurred by the partner

answer_html: Answer: (A) The fixed remuneration agreed to be paid to the partner is debited to Realization Account and credited to that partner's capital account[cite: 25].

question_html: What happens when a partner takes over an asset of the firm upon dissolution?

options.A: Partner's Capital Account is debited and Realization Account is credited[cite: 25]
options.B: Realization Account is debited and Partner's Capital credited

answer_html: Answer: (A) Partner's Capital Account is debited and Realization Account credited at the agreed valuation[cite: 25].

question_html: In the Highest Relative Capital Method of piecemeal distribution, which partner is paid off first?

options.A: The partner who has the higher relative capital in proportion to his profit-sharing ratio[cite: 25]
options.B: The partner with the lowest capital balance

answer_html: Answer: (A) The partner who has the higher relative capital in proportion to his profit-sharing ratio is paid off first until capitals are reduced to profit-sharing ratio[cite: 25].

question_html: What is the fundamental premise of the Maximum Loss Method in piecemeal distribution?

options.A: Each installment realized is considered to be the final payment, assuming remaining assets and claims are worthless[cite: 25]
options.B: Assets are assumed to realize book value
options.C: No payments are made until all assets are fully sold
options.D: Losses are distributed equally among all partners

answer_html: Answer: (A) Each installment realized is considered the final payment, treating outstanding assets as worthless and calculating maximum possible loss[cite: 25].

question_html: What are the legal consequences regarding the estate of an insolvent partner upon adjudication?

options.A: The estate of the insolvent partner is not liable for any act of the firm after the date of the order of adjudication[cite: 25]
options.B: The estate remains fully liable for all future debts indefinitely
options.C: The estate is seized by the other partners immediately without court order
options.D: The estate takes over management of the firm

answer_html: Answer: (A) The estate of the insolvent partner is not liable for any act of the firm after the date of the order of adjudication[cite: 25].

question_html: When does a partnership firm stand dissolved automatically due to insolvency?

options.A: When all partners except one become insolvent[cite: 25]
options.B: When any single partner becomes insolvent

answer_html: Answer: (A) A firm stands dissolved when all partners except one become insolvent[cite: 25].

question_html: What is the effect of the business of a firm becoming illegal on the partnership?

options.A: The firm stands dissolved compulsorily[cite: 25]
options.B: The firm can continue with court permission

answer_html: Answer: (A) A firm stands dissolved if the business becomes illegal[cite: 25].

question_html: In the case of a partnership at will, how can dissolution be brought about by a partner?

options.A: By giving notice of dissolution to other partners[cite: 25]
options.B: By filing an immediate bankruptcy petition
options.D: By transferring share to a third party

answer_html: Answer: (A) In case of partnership at will, a firm stands dissolved when a partner gives notice of dissolution[cite: 25].

question_html: Under what judicial circumstance can the court order dissolution of a firm based on business viability?

options.A: Where the business cannot be carried on except at a loss[cite: 25]
options.D: Where fixed assets appreciate in value

answer_html: Answer: (A) The court has the option to order dissolution where the business cannot be carried on except at a loss[cite: 25].
topic_text: Court Order on Business at a Loss

question_html: What is the correct accounting treatment when a provision against an asset (such as Provision for Doubtful Debts) appears on dissolution?

options.A: Transferred to the credit side of Realization Account[cite: 25]
options.C: Transferred to Partners' Capital Accounts directly

answer_html: Answer: (A) Provisions and reserves against assets are transferred to the credit side of Realization Account[cite: 25].

question_html: How are accumulated profits or general reserves shown in the balance sheet treated upon dissolution?

options.A: Transferred to partners' capital accounts in their profit-sharing ratio[cite: 25]
options.D: Written off to P&L Suspense Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Accumulated profits and general reserves are transferred to capital accounts in the profit-sharing ratio and are not sent to Realization Account[cite: 25].

question_html: What does the balance of the Cash/Bank Account represent at the very end of the dissolution process?

options.A: It will be exactly equal to the credit balances of partners' capital accounts, enabling final payout[cite: 25]
options.B: It will show a net realization profit
options.C: It will be equal to third-party creditors

answer_html: Answer: (A) The balance of the cash account at the end will be exactly equal to the balance of capital accounts, provided they are in credit, to close accounts[cite: 25].
topic_text: Cash Account Final Balance on Dissolution

question_html: What is the statutory provision regarding a partner transferring their interest or share in the partnership to a third party?

options.A: It gives the court the option to order dissolution of the firm[cite: 25]
options.B: It automatically dissolves the firm without court order
options.C: It is strictly prohibited and void ab initio
options.D: It makes the third party a full partner automatically

answer_html: Answer: (A) The court has the option to order dissolution where a partner transfers his interest or share to a third party[cite: 25].
topic_text: Transfer of Interest and Court Dissolution

question_html: In an LLP winding up, if an LLP has failed to file its statement of accounts and solvency or annual returns for how many consecutive financial years with the Registrar can the Tribunal initiate winding up?

options.A: More than five consecutive financial years[cite: 25]

answer_html: Answer: (A) Tribunal may initiate winding up if LLP fails to submit statements of accounts and solvency or annual returns for more than five consecutive financial years[cite: 25].
